claim.pdf_says: Rows printed indented under their parents: phrases under "PERFORM statement"; "TEST BEFORE/AFTER phrase" further indented under "UNTIL phrase" and again under "VARYING phrase"; "AFTER phrase" under "VARYING phrase"; "Maximum of two AFTER phrases" and "At least 6 AFTER phrases permitted" under "AFTER phrase"; READ, RECEIVE and RELEASE phrases under their statements.
claim.why_it_matters: The hierarchy is flattened: the two 'TEST BEFORE/AFTER phrase' rows lose their parents (UNTIL vs VARYING), and 'Maximum of two AFTER phrases' reads as a PERFORM-level element rather than a limit on the AFTER phrase. Adjacent pages preserve indentation with  . Values are correct.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of page 744 (XVII-36) prints the ELEMENT column with four indentation levels: statements flush left (PERFORM, PURGE, READ, RECEIVE, RELEASE); their phrases one step in; 'TEST BEFORE/AFTER phrase' two steps in under UNTIL and again under VARYING; 'AFTER phrase' and the two 'Identifier-2/Identifier-5' ordering rows two steps in under VARYING; 'Maximum of two AFTER phrases' and 'At least 6 AFTER phrases permitted' three steps in under AFTER. The markdown table has no indentation in any row, so all levels flatten to one and only shorter dot leaders hint at the nesting. Elsewhere the transcription marks nesting in these difference tables with leading   (for example specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 1512 onward), so this page is inconsistent with that convention. The lost nesting changes meaning: the two identical 'TEST BEFORE/AFTER phrase' rows cannot be told apart (UNTIL versus VARYING), and the AFTER-phrase limits and the identifier-2/identifier-5 ordering rows lose their parent. Every 2ND STD/3RD STD value matches the print. The claim quotes both sources correctly.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate, with one addition: the flattening covers the whole table, not only the rows quoted. Every child row on the page lost its indentation, including PERFORM's first-level phrases, the identifier-2/identifier-5 ordering rows (second level, under VARYING), and the READ, RECEIVE and RELEASE phrases. Values are correct; only the hierarchy is missing.
